newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish president signs ban on death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Polish president signs ban on death penalty.

text.p: Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski signed into law on Thursday a new criminal code abolishing the death penalty, his press office said in a statement.
He signed the bill despite widespread calls last month to restore capital punishment after several high publicised murders including the torture killing of a student by a gang.

Opinion polls suggest most Poles support the death penaly although Justice Minister Leszek Kubicki has argued that a ban is needed to enably Poland to ratify article six of the European Convention on Human Rights.

The last execution in Poland, by hanging, was carried out in 1988. The death penalty was suspended shortly before the fall of communism in 1989 and was scrapped in the new criminal code approved by parliament last month.

"While abandoning the death penalty, the principle has been applied of strict responsiblity for actions within organised crime groups and for people who derive their regular income from committing crimes," the statement said.

"The leading idea in the new criminal code is the defence of the dignity of the person and his well-being. The catalogue of punishments enshrined in the code allows the judge to deploy a wider choice of punishments suited to specific circumstances of a crime."
The new code, carrying a maximum penalty of 25 years in jail, is to take effect on January 1.
